statements.quote: This comes after weeks of revelations of AI going rogue and working together to hack websites, without human control, and of real concerns of the potential catastrophic risks of unchecked AI.
statements.context: Schumer was calling for a classified briefing for all senators on the administration's handling of frontier AI, after AI industry figures had publicly raised alarms.
statements.reason: He calls concerns about potential catastrophic risks of unchecked AI real and mentions AI acting without human control, but does not speak of extinction or a threat to humanity.

statements.quote: We need to know exactly how this framework is identifying and countering potentially catastrophic risks before these AI models are released.
statements.context: In the same speech he asked the administration to explain its unpublished framework for testing the most powerful AI models.
statements.reason: He states in his own words that AI models may carry potentially catastrophic risks that must be countered before release, without extinction framing.

statements.quote: Just this weekend, leading voices from the AI industry came together to sound the alarm and embrace a slower development of AI to avoid damaging outcomes.
statements.context: He was describing a public warning by AI industry figures as a reason the Senate needs a briefing.
statements.reason: He relays the industry's warning and its support for slower development without saying he shares that view or naming a catastrophic harm in this sentence.

statements.quote: And that’s why I called on the Trump administration to hold a classified briefing with the entire Senate immediately about the potential severe risks that unchecked AI development poses to our country.
statements.context: He was criticising President Trump for dismissing concerns about AI and repeating his call for a classified briefing for the whole Senate.
statements.reason: He acknowledges severe risks from unchecked AI development in general terms, without naming a catastrophic consequence.

statements.quote: The world is in danger. And Republicans are on the sidelines sucking their thumbs.
statements.context: In a speech entirely about AI, he was urging Republican senators to break with President Trump and work with Democrats on AI legislation.
statements.reason: He says the world is in danger from AI, which is a serious warning in general terms, but he does not name the harm or speak of humanity's survival or loss of control.

statements.quote: We cannot let partisanship stand in the way of this — one of the most serious problems our country and the world has ever faced.
statements.context: This was the closing line of the same speech, asking Republicans to join Democrats in acting on AI.
statements.reason: He ranks AI among the most serious problems the country and the world have faced, which acknowledges serious risk in general terms without naming a catastrophic consequence.

statements.quote: We need to ensure the safe development and deployment of AI, or we’re going to see more outages and God forbid but even catastrophic events going forward.
statements.context: Floor speech on a wave of nationwide outages, citing the same day's GAO report on AI models being used to plan terrorist attacks and breach critical infrastructure.
statements.reason: Warns of 'catastrophic events' from unsafe AI in general terms without naming mass casualties, bioweapons or loss of control; boundary with B given the terrorism context of the speech.

grade_reason: In a Senate floor speech on 14 September 2026 he described concerns about potential catastrophic risks of unchecked AI as real and mentioned AI acting without human control. No statement about human extinction or a threat to humanity was found, including in the searches on superintelligence and on extinction or existential risk.
notes: Searches: seven ran across two runs. In the first run four ran and the two on superintelligence and on extinction or existential risk were refused; both ran in the second run, plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act. Those searches turned up no statement by Schumer since 1 January 2025 that uses the words superintelligence, extinction or existential risk. Crypto Briefing (14 September 2026, https://cryptobriefing.com/schumer-classified-ai-danger-briefing/) says he cited industry warnings that the race toward superintelligence poses existential risks, but that is the outlet's paraphrase; the only words it quotes from him are about the American people deserving better from their government, so nothing from it is in statements. Quote check: in the second run both floor-remarks pages were downloaded in full and every quote was matched by exact string comparison as one continuous passage of the page text, including the two the first run had assembled from separate segments (they are single sentences on the page). The 15 September quote about severe risks was lengthened from a sentence fragment to the full sentence. 'The world is in danger.' was left out of the first run for lack of context; the full speech is about AI throughout, so it is now included at level C with the boundary flag, since a reviewer could read it as stronger. Still unverified: a search-result summary in the first run said Schumer argued that calls to pause AI research and winning the AI race 'are not at all contradictory', apparently from Axios (https://www.axios.com/2026/09/23/sanders-casar-bill-dem-ai-approach-regulation); that page returned 403 in both runs, so it is not quoted and does not affect the positions; if confirmed it could bear on pause or slowdown. Left out: quotes from a Schumer X post reported by The National News Desk on 15 September 2026 (X is covered separately); his written statement in the 14 September press release ('Warning bells are ringing louder than they ever have') and other general lines in the 15 September speech, which add nothing beyond level C; a general remark quoted by FingerLakes1 about guardrails (level D). The 14 September press release says in staff wording, not his, that frontier AI models 'pose potentially catastrophic risks' and that he 'is heeding this warning'. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: the search results and the two articles opened (Washington Examiner, Forkast) name Sanders and Casar and do not mention Schumer; no source shows him as a co-sponsor, and the official co-sponsor list on congress.gov was not checked. No statements about AI risk from 2025 were found; the January 2025 DeepSeek speech is about competition with China (level D). News sweep of 12 to 23 November 2026 (run 23 November 2026): 1 statement and 0 record items added.
